newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SRI LANKA SETS RECORD SCORE IN TEST CRICKET

Sri Lankan cricketers scored the most runs in a test innings when they made 952 for six in the drawn match against India at Colombo on Wednesday. They beat the previous 1938 record of 903 runs by England against Australia. Sanath Jayasuriya made 340, Roshan Mahanama 225, Aravinda de Silva 125, Arjuna Ranatunga 86 and debutante Mahela Jayawardena another 66. Sanath Jayasuriya, who failed to break Brian Lara's record of 375 runs, became the fourth highest test scorer after Lara, Garfield Sobers and Len Hutton. -------
The decision to retire 10 billion rupees worth of treasury bills has been welcomed by the Sri Lankan business as a move that would stabilise interest rates.

Mano Selvanathan, chairman of Ceylon Chamber of Commerce, said the move reflected the government's positive outlook and prudent fiscal policy management. Dr. N.U. Jayawardene, a senior economist, described the the move as "very desirable" and said that the excessive public debt should be further reduced by utilising privatisation proceeds.
SUBSTANDARD VACCINE CAUSES FEAR OF WHOOPING COUGH EPIDEMIC
A whooping cough (Pertissus) epidemic among children might be on the rise again in Sri Lanka due to the use of substandard vaccine, Sri Lanka College of Paediatricians has warned.
UNHCR SAYS LTTE BLOCKING AID TO REFUGEES

The UNHCR said in a statement on Wednesday that talks held with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam for providing escort to ships carrying food and refugees had been inconclusive. Shipping services in the north stalled following two LTTE attacks on refugee and food vessels.
USAID PROVIDES GRANT TO MEDICINS SANS FRONTIERES (MSF)
United States Agency for International Development (USAID) has granted a five million rupee grant to MSF to provide medical assistance to the northern Jaffna Teaching Hospital.
